# GhostURL
 
> Privacy-first, ephemeral link sharing, end-to-end encrypted secret notes, and zero-storage WebRTC peer-to-peer file transfer.

## About

GhostURL is an open-source, account-less, privacy-preserving sharing utility. It combines self-destructing short links backed by Redis hardware TTL auto-eviction, end-to-end encrypted secret notes (GhostPaste), and direct browser-to-browser file beaming (GhostDrop) over encrypted WebRTC DataChannels with zero persistent server storage.

## Capabilities

- **Quick Bridge (Self-Destructing Short Links)**: Account-less, expiring short links with preset or custom timers (5 minutes up to 7 days). Supports Burn-on-Read visit quotas (1-view burn, 3 views, 5 views), client-side end-to-end encryption, and optional salted bcrypt passcode protection.
- **GhostPaste (Encrypted Secret Notes)**: Share passwords, private credentials, or code snippets with syntax highlighting. Automatically encrypted in the browser with AES-256-GCM where the decryption key is kept in the URL hash fragment. Completely invisible to backend servers and databases.
- **Anti-Crawler Safe Burn Defense**: Automated chat and social preview crawlers (Slack, Discord, WhatsApp, Telegram, Twitter, Facebook) are served static metadata without triggering view counts or incinerating single-use secrets. Human visitors confirm intent through a tactile Slide-to-Reveal gate.
- **Duress Passcode ("Poison Pill")**: Optional secondary passcode configured at creation. If entered under coercion, it instantly purges the link from Redis memory and serves an identical 404 response for plausible deniability.
- **Zero-Knowledge Delivery Status Receipt**: Senders receive a private cryptographic receipt token to verify whether their link is pending, viewed, or burned, without recording recipient IP addresses or tracking cookies.
- **Nearby Radar (Zero-Setup P2P Link & Text Transfer)**: Instant local-network device discovery with 6-digit room code fallback for cellular/remote peers. Direct encrypted client-to-client transfer over WebRTC DataChannels.
- **GhostDrop (Zero-Storage P2P File Beaming)**: Direct browser-to-browser streaming for files of arbitrary size with dual-engine flow control (WebRTC DataChannels + WebSocket signaling relay fallback). Zero server, disk, or database retention.

## Security & Privacy Invariants

- **Zero-Knowledge Client-Side Encryption**: Symmetric AES-256-GCM keys are held strictly in the URL hash fragment (`#k=...`). Per HTTP specifications, browsers never transmit hash fragments to servers.
- **Atomic Burn-on-Read**: Single-use links and notes are atomically deleted upon reading.
- **Plausible Deniability**: Entering a duress passcode deletes stored records and yields standard 404 Not Found responses identical to non-existent links.
- **Zero Database Persistence for File Transfers**: WebRTC DataChannels and signaling streams stream directly between browser memories; nothing is saved on servers.
- **Ephemeral Auto-Destruction**: Links auto-expire via native Redis in-memory TTL; no background cron jobs or orphaned records.
- **Salted Bcrypt Passcodes**: Link passcodes and duress passcodes are salted and hashed with `bcrypt.DefaultCost`.
- **Zero Client IP Logging**: Public IPs are evaluated only transiently in memory to group local devices and never logged to disk.
- **Cookieless Telemetry**: Privacy-first, GDPR-compliant analytics without storing IP addresses or PII.

## Key Pages

- [Home / App](https://www.ghosturl.web.id/): Main application interface for creating ephemeral links and beaming files via GhostDrop.

## Technical Specifications

- Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS
- Backend: Go 1.22+, Gin Framework, Gorilla WebSocket
- Datastore: Redis 7 (In-Memory RAM with native EXPIRE)
- P2P Protocols: WebRTC DataChannels (binary streaming), STUN negotiation
